Research design

Research question

How are research materials described in this saved Bologna coding record?

Case definition

This English teaching subset contains selected translated passages from three public Bologna interviews. The Notebook covers all excerpts selected from interview02.txt, not the full original interview.

Method and decisions

Method used: Qualitative Content Analysis

Analytic approach

Qualitative Content Analysis

Analysis unit

An existing quotation and its saved code path, read in the context of the full source document.

Approach and decisions

This is a worked software example using translated Bologna excerpts and source-linked teaching associations. Translated offsets refer to the English teaching documents, not the Italian originals. This is not a new empirical analysis. Table labels retain the saved ancestry. Method steps show the workflow; unchecked review stages remain unconfirmed.

Method map M1 · Qualitative Content Analysis

Procedure overview, not a completion record. Record your approach and decisions; researcher confirmations remain separate.

  1. 01Declare unit and approachDocument what is analysed and the chosen content analysis approach.
  2. 02Select meaning unitsIdentify relevant passages while retaining their surrounding context.
  3. 03Condense when appropriateShorten meaning units only when this fits the analytic design.
  4. 04Code and review categoriesCompare codes and refine categories with explicit analytic decisions.
  5. 05Interpret in contextConsider meaning and abstraction; themes are optional, design-dependent.
  6. 06Write with evidenceConnect categories, interpretation and source quotations in the report.

Revisit 05 → 02 · Select meaning units

Content analysis is a complete method. It is not a compulsory preliminary stage for TA or Comparative QCA.

Review and limitations

Counterexamples and variation

Only selected material-related passages are interpreted here. Contrasting perspectives across the other interviews require further contextual reading.

Limitations

This small writing example does not establish a complete analysis or saturation. Counts describe saved coding activity rather than importance or prevalence among people.

Reflexivity

The short illustrative narrative was prepared for the QT demonstration. It is not an independently validated analysis of this corpus.

Quality and review

Quoted characters and code identities were checked against the saved source. All five figures use only this three-document translated teaching subset and the unchanged counting rules.

Research and assistance disclosure

Public Bologna CC0 data only. No private interviews or model calls were used. Editing the downloaded Word documents does not change the QT project.

E1 interview02-english-excerpts.txt

This is [something new] compared with when I began this kind of research. Fifteen years ago I would of course have had to go to the library. Now one edition has been digitised by Google Books, while for the 1502 edition we used the digitised print from the Bavarian State Library in Munich, which is an exceptional repository of early printed books. Seventy per cent of what we look for among incunabula, late-fifteenth-century printed books and sixteenth-century editions can be found there.
